data.content:
## Root cause

The two commands aren't inconsistent — the translate step genuinely failed to fix the drift, but silently.

`docs/scripts/check-locale-drift.ts` correctly found 40 untranslated prose units in `docs/api/css/responsive.md` for locale `se` (Northern Sami). When you ran `docs:locales:translate:copilot`, the `docs:api:locales:copilot` step batches prose strings into character-budget chunks (default 4000 chars, [api-translation.ts](docs/scripts/api-translation.ts#L423)) and translates each chunk with one CLI call under a 120s timeout ([api-translation.ts](docs/scripts/api-translation.ts#L500)). The `responsive.md` batch (40 CSS-heavy technical strings, translated into a low-resource language) exceeded that timeout, so it was skipped with a line like:

```
! skipped a batch of 40 strings: AI command timed out after 120000ms for batch of 40 strings
```

That's logged but non-fatal — the script still exits 0 and prints "no drift" for everything it did manage, so the failure is easy to miss among hundreds of "cached" lines.

I reproduced it, then confirmed the fix: rerunning just that locale with a longer timeout translated all 40 units successfully and cleared the drift:

```bash
cd docs
DOCS_TRANSLATION_LOCALE=se DOCS_TRANSLATION_TIMEOUT_MS=300000 \
  DOCS_TRANSLATION_COMMAND_ARGS="--model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 --effort low --strict-mcp-config --setting-sources user" \
  node scripts/build-api-locales.ts
node scripts/check-locale-drift.ts   # ✓ no translation drift
```

Only [l10n/se/docs.api.po](l10n/se/docs.api.po) changed (the 40 filled `msgstr` entries + revision timestamp) — that's already applied in your working tree, ready to commit alongside a changeset.

**Note:** I also confirmed the `copilot-wrapper.sh` + `gpt-5-mini --effort low` adapter separately fails on these same strings by returning the English text unchanged (correctly rejected by the passthrough guard, not a corruption risk, just doesn't fix it) — so for `se`, prefer the claude adapter with a longer timeout.

---
"@pantoken/pendo": patch
---

Fix the igniteai banner glyph resolving to an empty computed value in production. `scripts/embed.ts`'s `productIcons` list was missing `"igniteai"`, so `--instui-logo-igniteai-icon-reversed` was referenced by `container.css` but never embedded into the shipped `global.css`/bundle.

data.content:
## Summary

`--_banner-glyph: var(--instui-logo-igniteai-icon-reversed)` resolved to empty in production because the token itself was never defined in the shipped CSS — only referenced.

**Root cause:** [renderers/pendo/scripts/embed.ts](renderers/pendo/scripts/embed.ts#L13) builds the `productLogoCss` block (the actual `url(...)` data-URI definitions) from a hardcoded `productIcons` list containing `canvas`, `parchment`, `mastery`, `learnplatform` — but not `igniteai`, even though `container.css` has an `-igniteai` banner variant referencing that token. So `dist/global.css` contained `var(--ly)` (minified name) with no matching `--ly: url(...)` definition anywhere.

**Fix:** added `"igniteai"` to `productIcons`, then regenerated `generated/embedded.ts`, `generated/global.css`, and rebuilt `dist/` — verified the definition now exists and resolves in the built output. Added a changeset for `@pantoken/pendo`.

Note: `vp test` has one pre-existing, unrelated failing test in `tests/build.test.ts` (an `:is(:scope[class*="instui-alert"], ...)` selector assertion that doesn't match the current alert-section markup) — confirmed via `git stash` that it fails independently of this change, so I left it alone.
